chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-ʿIs ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about a man who went out during the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating suhoor in a house. He looked at the dawn and called out to them that dawn had indeed risen. So some stopped, while some thought that he was joking, and so he ate. He said: “He completes the fast and makes it up.”

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, the time when eating becomes forbidden for the fasting person
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the prescribed time of obligatory sawm
key_terms.يَتَسَحَّرُونَ: they were taking the pre-dawn meal before the fast
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up the fast on another day
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he completes the fast for the remainder of the day

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone eats after dawn in Ramadan thinking the warning was a joke?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who continues eating after true dawn in Ramadan because he assumed the warning was not serious. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the person must continue the fast for the day and also perform qada' for it afterward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1939 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who, during the Month of Ramadan, went out while his companions were taking suhoor (pre-dawn meal) in a house. He saw the dawn and called out to them, saying that the dawn had risen. Some of them stopped eating, while others thought he was joking and continued to eat.
Imam (as) said: 'They must complete their fast and make up another day.'"
